name: Adoniram
overview: Adoniram was a male figure in the biblical narrative known for his leadership role over the men subjected to forced labor. Scripture identifies him specifically in this administrative capacity, highlighting his responsibility in overseeing significant labor forces. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this role.
namesAndTitles: The name Adoniram means '[my] lord is exalted,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that points to the sovereignty of God. This proper name, as recorded, is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries a significant declaration of divine exaltation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Adoniram was the son of Abda, establishing a direct familial relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections are noted in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Adoniram's significance in Scripture stems from his administrative oversight of forced laborers, a critical function in the governance and organization of the kingdom's workforce. His leadership role, as noted in 1 Kings 4:6, situates him within the broader context of Solomon's administration and the execution of royal duties. This position underscores the practical aspects of kingdom management under divine providence.
